Implemented the Python port.

What’s included:
- [zip_password_finder.py](C:/Users/liuliu/Documents/tura_workspace/target/project-rebuild-source-port/r-6aaa870ba0/zip-password-finder/codex-main-1/workspace/zip_password_finder.py): CLI parsing, charset/dictionary/mask generation, ZIP validation, AES verifier, ZipCrypto fallback.
- [executable](C:/Users/liuliu/Documents/tura_workspace/target/project-rebuild-source-port/r-6aaa870ba0/zip-password-finder/codex-main-1/workspace/executable): POSIX-style runnable entrypoint.
- [executable.cmd](C:/Users/liuliu/Documents/tura_workspace/target/project-rebuild-source-port/r-6aaa870ba0/zip-password-finder/codex-main-1/workspace/executable.cmd): Windows runnable entrypoint.
- [compile.sh](C:/Users/liuliu/Documents/tura_workspace/target/project-rebuild-source-port/r-6aaa870ba0/zip-password-finder/codex-main-1/workspace/compile.sh): now marks `./executable` runnable.

Verified against the official binary for help/version, missing/invalid args, duplicate args, dictionary mode, mask mode, brute force mode, and multi-file auto-selection. The deterministic stdout/stderr lines and exit statuses match; elapsed timing values naturally differ between processes. Local `sh`/`bash` is not installed in this Windows workspace, so I could not execute `compile.sh` here, but the produced `.\executable` and `.\executable.cmd` smoke tests pass.
